Any disruption in our supply chain due to such farmer defaults or disputes could require us to procure processed-grade potatoes from alternate sources at higher prices, or could result in shortfall in meeting customer requirements.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Contract Farming: Global Scenario The global market for contract farming is estimated to be valued at USD 61.5 Bn in CY 2024, growing by a CAGR of nearly 3.2% between 2021 and 2024.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Going ahead, the global market for contract farming is expected to increase by CAGR of 3.5% between CY 2024 and 2030 to reach USD 75.6 Bn.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Source: D&B Research, CY – Calendar Year, 2030F – 2030 Forecast 55.9 61.5 75.6 CY 2021 CY 2024 CY 2030F Global Contract Farming Market Size (in USD Bn) CAGR: 3.2% CAGR: 3.5% Contract Farming Landscape in India Contract farming in India has emerged as a significant mechanism to strengthen the agricultural sector, enhance productivity, and create structured frameworks for farmer-market linkages.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: India Market Size & Growth Prospects Indian market for contract farming is estimated to be valued at USD 7.0 Bn in FY 2025.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: During the time FY 2021-25, the Indian market for contract farming has increased by a CAGR of nearly 6.7%.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Going ahead, the industry is expected to reach a value of USD 9.7 Bn by FY 2030, registering a CAGR of 6.8% between FY 2025 and 2030.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: From CY 2018 to CY 2027, the growth in cultivated land is at a moderate pace of 1.8% CAGR, while the growth in area under contract farming is much higher at 8.3% CAGR, indicating an increasing trend in the adoption of contract farming.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: The short-term CAGR (CY 2025- CY 2027) for cultivated land is 1.91%, whereas the CAGR for contract farming is projected to be significantly higher at 10.40%.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: This suggests a rapid growth in contract farming adoption in the next few years. 5.4 7.0 9.7 FY 2021 FY 2025E FY 2030F Indian Contract Farming Market Size (in USD Bn) CAGR: 6.8% CAGR: 6.7% Source: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Key Products Currently Covered Under Contract Farming in India Contract farming has seen significant growth in India in recent years, especially in high-demand crops like tomato, onion, and fruits.

other_material_facts.value: While the export of potatoes, seed potatoes, and related products currently represents just 1.05% of the country’s overall production, export volumes have exhibited a robust growth trajectory, with a CAGR of 14.1% over the past two decades.

other_material_facts.label: working_capital
other_material_facts.value: Working Capital Profile Our Company operates with a positive working capital cycle, driven by procurement of seed potatoes, payments to farmers, storage costs, and receivables from farmers, processing units and institutional buyers.

other_material_facts.label: working_capital
other_material_facts.value: This working capital structure indicates that receivable cycles and inventory buildup are longer than payable cycles, resulting in higher funding requirements.

other_material_facts.label: working_capital
other_material_facts.value: Delays in collections or increases in storage periods may elongate the working capital cycle, while improvements in procurement scheduling and receivable realization could ease the liquidity burden.

other_material_facts.label: working_capital
other_material_facts.value: Extended holding periods tie up working capital and increase storage costs.

other_material_facts.label: working_capital
other_material_facts.value: Efficient management of inventory turnover, aligned with demand forecasts and processing schedules, remains critical to maintaining an optimal working capital structure.

other_material_facts.label: debt_repayment
other_material_facts.value: A reduction in supplier credit terms or simultaneous elongation of receivable cycles may increase reliance on borrowings or internal accruals.
